item.title: m-3: sc-agent-log and digest() into sc-agent-sqlite

results.statement: Every core table's SQL is defined in `sc-agent-schema` and nowhere else.
results.explanation: This bead does not carry the directive forward.

results.statement: In production runs, every logger sc-agent creates by default, not injected by a caller, must write under the configured log root with a fixed folder and file name, so tools can find the logs.
results.quote: I mandated - that all default loggers created in production have root/folder/file naming conventions specified.
results.deterministic_check: test: default_logger(name) path == `<log_root>/logs/<name>.log.jsonl`; session sink path == `<log_root>/sessions/<repo-id>/<role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl`
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.16); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: In sc-agent code, related values passed to several methods must be grouped in one struct that replaces those repeated parameters, so encapsulation is efficient and repeated code stays minimal as the architecture scales.
results.quote: Related values are strategically grouped in one struct to remove repeated method parameters, for efficient encapsulation and to minimize repeated code as the architecture scales.
results.deterministic_check: review of changed pub fn signatures: no function takes run_id/tool/tool_version/cache/model/provider as separate params
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.52); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: A rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, model resolution and the like) must be specified only in sc-agent's records; a derivative tool's records (judge-jev, plan-anchor and others) must not restate it and give only the tool name and the tool's own behaviour, so each rule has one source.
results.quote: judge-jev and plan-anchor simply supply tool name and follow the rules established for all decidr based tools
results.context: planning session; session, 2026-11-26; also: 'same thing for REQ-JEV-0009 (this is sc-agent requirement) and applies to all tools'
results.deterministic_check: no derivative-tool record states log placement, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields; each points to the sc-agent record
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.49); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: When a caller passes its own sc_observability Logger into an sc-agent wheel call, sc-agent must not build a second Logger for that log.
results.quote: we created a oversized set of sprints expressly to normalize config and logging around sc-observability logger (injected).  why do you keep adding more loggers to the design? ... add a new anchor banning python_logger ... lock this
results.deterministic_check: no LoggerBuilder call in crates/sc-agent-py runs on a path where the caller supplied a logger
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.58); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: The general log is written through sc-observability under its rotation and deletion policy; sc-agent adds no retention rule of its own.
results.quote: general logs follow sc-obs rotation/deletion guidelines
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.06); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: The session schema stores a request once in `messages`, keyed by sha256, and each model reply as a row in `responses` that references it.
results.quote: We likely want message+sha256 and response+model in separate tables as this is one->many
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.34); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: A cache hit is decided by the request sha256 and the model alone; `run_id` is not part of the cache key.
results.quote: run-id has nothing to do with caching. run is a collection of queries of which some may be cached (if caching enabled)
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.24); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: judge-jev, plan-anchor and every other sc-agent-based tool store their results in the repository's SQLite database, not in JSON or JSONL result files.
results.quote: At the end of the day, I want all the 'results' from plan-anchor, judge-jev or any other app to save data to SQLite.
results.explanation: Jev was not confident (min confidence 0.56); the anchor or the bead may be underspecified.

results.statement: sc-agent writes each session row to the repository's SQLite database through `sc-agent-sqlite`; no code writes `sessions.jsonl`.
results.quote: I want session logs written to SQLite, jsonl was just a quick item for mvp

results.statement: sc-agent tests must not depend on races, wall-clock timing, sleeps, event-loop ordering or system load; a test found to depend on one must be redesigned to drive its logic with controlled inputs.
results.quote: Flaky tests are prohibited by design. Any flaky test identified (one that relies on a race, timing, sleeps, event-loop ordering or load) must be re-designed to be deterministic by driving the logic with controlled inputs.
results.deterministic_check: review changed tests for sleep, wall-clock assertions, poll-until-timeout and unsynchronized thread ordering; a failure-only backstop that fails with captured output is allowed
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.
